shortDescription: Real-time delay tracking and GTFS trip analytics dashboard for GO Transit's Barrie Line, deployed to Cloudflare Pages with Supabase.
techStack: GitHub Actions (workflows for GTFS refresh & trip ID resolution)
architectureRules: Frontend data client in src/lib/supabase.js points to Supabase using public VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY; table name constant is exported as TABLE ('go_train_delays').
Queries strictly select ALERT_COLUMNS to exclude sensitive and bulky raw email payloads (such as raw_body) from client fetches.
Calendar and daily queries must use Toronto time (torontoToday() via Intl.DateTimeFormat 'en-CA' with 'America/Toronto') rather than UTC to avoid evening date mismatches.
Delay observations are deduped using dedupeToLatestObservations() keyed on observation_key and ordered by received_at to reflect latest update stages without duplicate counting.
GTFS reference data (routes, stops, trips, stop_times, calendar) is refreshed weekly via scripts/refresh_gtfs.py and used by Supabase RPC resolve_trip_ids() to map delays to specific train runs.

Metrolinx Open API integration requires an isolated ingestion path and new dedicated Supabase tables/views to decouple from the legacy email-based 'go_train_delays' table and Cloudflare Worker pipeline.
liveRules: Timezone shifts: GTFS departure times past midnight are encoded as >= 24:00:00 (e.g. 24:40:00) and belong to the preceding service date (service_date - 1).
Date parsing: 'YYYY-MM-DD' service_date strings must be parsed into local dates (as done in parseServiceDate) rather than new Date(str) which defaults to UTC midnight.
Heatmap data isolation: Heatmaps require an independent ~84-90 day window (CALENDAR_WINDOW_DAYS) rather than adopting the active incident feed filter.
Supabase RLS: The frontend uses the anonymous key which is read-only; table inserts, batch updates, and resolve_trip_ids RPC require SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY.

GO Transit Open API documentation mentioned in user prompt was not provided in the repo files; ingestion scripts/endpoints will need the target Metrolinx API schema (e.g., ServiceUpdates, NextService, or GTFS-RT feeds) and request headers.
